analysis:
All three changed files are test-only: AdmissionRateEstimatorTests.swift (added), EngineMeasurementOrderingTests.swift (added) and LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift (a new test at lines 181-200). No production source, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, encryption or cache-storage code is modified in the supplied units, so no threat-model asset, boundary or mitigation changes here.

What the tests exercise: TTFT admission-rate estimation (IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate, the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES kill switch, and the decode-shape EWMA) and ordering of engine measurement observations. Both are availability and performance heuristics. They sit near TB-007 and T-010/T-029, as DoS and scheduling behaviour rather than confidentiality or integrity. The tests use a scripted engine and synthetic data, with no real keys, prompts or secrets.

The LaunchAgent test asserts that the rollback env key reaches the provider job's plist via inferencePassthroughEnvKeys. It checks that the key is not forwarded to the watchdog, and that unrelated env vars such as UNRELATED_SECRET are filtered out. This reinforces an allowlist, not a widening. The env passthrough is a local-operator control (TB-003), and an operator can already set the process environment, so it adds no new attack surface.

Unverified contract: the production implementations (DeadlineAdmissionFixes, IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate, EnginePerformanceMeasurements ordering, and the LaunchAgent allowlist entry) are not in this batch. The tests assume that the allowlist change and the fail-open behaviour for stale evidence on an idle engine exist elsewhere in the PR. A reviewer of those source files should check that fail-open admission after stale evidence cannot be abused for resource exhaustion (T-029 class), and that late-observation timestamp handling cannot be manipulated by a provider to keep stale rates fresh. Neither is a defect visible here.
